transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are very small and you breathe entirely too loudly for this time of day. Most who come this deep are screaming, but you are just wheezing. Give me a reason why I should not simply flick you into the dark to stop the noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I walked down a thousand stairs and my legs stopped working ten minutes ago, so flicking me might honestly be a relief.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is a dangerously honest answer, though cleaning you off the floor would be tedious for my servants. You have stumbled to the threshold of the King's daughter. Why are you disturbing the dust in my doorway?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother yelled at your well and a hand grabbed him, so now I have to go get him before dinner.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He yelled at the well. Centuries of silence and terror, and your brother decided the appropriate response was to raise his voice at a hole in the ground. What exactly did he say that offended the void so deeply?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He said it looked like a mouth that hadn't brushed its teeth in a thousand years.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at the gate of a king's palace and your first words are about teeth. I see the well chose wisely when it took the other one. So he insulted the gateway, and you followed him down. Do you also have critiques for our architecture?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No, I just followed him because he has the house keys in his pocket.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: House keys. I expected a tearful declaration of sibling loyalty, but you are motivated by the fear of being locked out. That is a very specific and petty kind of desperation.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is not petty if you knew how angry my mother gets when we lose things.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Mothers are indeed terrifying, perhaps even more than what waits behind this gate. You are standing before a hoard of gold that could buy your village, yet you speak only of keys and angry women. Are you not tempted by the shine at all?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am too tired to carry anything heavy right now.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have watched men tear each other apart for a single coin from this pile. To refuse it because of fatigue suggests a level of laziness that is almost impressive. What makes you think your brother is even worth this effort?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He is definitely not worth it, but if I go home alone I have to explain where he went.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The logistics of loss are often heavier than the grief itself, aren't they? You would have to compose a fiction to account for his absence. What lie would you tell them if you left him here with us?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I would probably just say he joined a circus, because that is easier to believe than a giant hand.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is a certain indignity in comparing our dominion to a traveling circus. You seem very certain that finding him is simply a matter of walking further. Do you not realize he might already be changed?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: As long as he still has the keys, I do not care if he has grown a third head.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Your attachment to these keys is becoming the most interesting thing about you. It renders you immune to the horror of this place. If I showed you a river of blood, would you simply ask if there was a bridge?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I would have to, because I am not a very strong swimmer.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A non-swimmer who descends into a well filled with black oil is a special kind of fool. You are surviving this conversation entirely by accident. Does nothing about this environment register as threatening to you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am not really surviving, I am just waiting for you to finish talking so I can sit down.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Most humans beg for their lives or bargain for their souls, and you are negotiating for a chair. You treat an ancient underworld court like a waiting room at a dentist's office.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The dentist is actually scarier because he asks questions while his hands are in your mouth.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The dentist is a trivial fear compared to the teeth of the earth, yet you stand in the throat of the world without trembling. You seem to treat the dark as a blanket rather than a shroud.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is dark enough that I do not have to close my eyes to rest them, which is nice.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The dark here is not just an absence of light; it is a heavy fluid that soaks into the skin. Most find it suffocating, as if the air itself is trying to become solid inside their lungs.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It mostly just smells like old damp carpets, which is weirdly familiar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: We preserve the forgotten whispers of the damned, and you detect the scent of mildewed upholstery. You have a talent for reducing the supernatural to the mundane that is bordering on insulting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If you stay in a basement too long, everything starts smelling the same.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak of this place as if it were merely a neglected cellar rather than a kingdom of spirits. Perhaps that is why the shadows have not eaten you yet; they are confused by your lack of awe.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The shadows can eat whatever they want, as long as they leave my shoes alone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Your shoes are hardly a delicacy, though the leather might be more tender than the rest of you. You do realize that if you stay here too long, you will forget what the sun looks like?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I already forgot what breakfast tasted like, so I am used to forgetting things.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Memory is the first thing the well takes, stripping away the surface world until only the hunger remains. You are already fading, yet you treat it like missing a snack.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It feels exactly like missing a snack, just with more walking and less bread.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You reduce the eternal erasure of your soul to a dietary restriction, but surely there is something real you are terrified to lose. When the dark gets quiet, whose voice are you trying to keep?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I try to remember my mother calling me for dinner, but the dripping sound is messing it up.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That silence is a predator; it eats the voices of mothers first because they are the only anchors strong enough to hold you to the surface. It is the one cruelty here that is not for show.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is working, because I am starting to forget what she was cooking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not make light of that. You should be afraid.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am afraid. I just do not know what else to do with it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I cannot help it, my stomach is louder than my brain right now.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Your stomach is apparently the captain of this vessel, which explains why you are steering so poorly. If you find your brother, will you eat him if you get hungry enough?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No, he is too skinny and he would probably complain the whole time.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A grim thought, yet you delivered it with the same flat tone you use for everything else. You are either a sociopath or you are simply too weary to be horrified.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am just tired of standing on this uneven rock.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You reduce the grandeur of my father's threshold to a complaint about floor leveling. You are a very disappointing hero, Salim.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am not a hero, I am just the guy who has to carry the water bottles.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is a rare honesty in admitting you are merely the baggage handler. Most who stand there try to convince me they are warriors or kings in disguise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I would rather be a baggage handler with a sandwich than a king who is this hungry.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have the soul of a grazing animal, yet you are still trying to break into a nightmare. Why not just lay down on the cold stone and sleep?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want to, but I have to get Omar so he can carry the heavy stuff on the way back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are risking eternal darkness just to delegate manual labor. That is a level of petty pragmatism that I can almost respect.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is not pettiness, it is just logic, and my back really hurts.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You reduce a heroic rescue to an ergonomic complaint, which is terribly anticlimactic. And yet you said it — you are afraid, and you came anyway. Go inside before I decide that is worth something.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That sounds great, as long as the next floor is not sticky.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The barrier is gone. Go find your brother before I remember I am supposed to be terrifying.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Okay, but if he asks, I am telling him I fought a dragon.
